item.text: {"text":"Single-negative BCE is a plausible bottleneck, but evidence does not establish an Electronics-specific failure. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) links sampled-BCE overconfidence to poorer ranking and combines multiple negatives with generalized BCE; recommended defaults are 128–256 negatives and calibration parameter t=0.75, trading accuracy against memory and training time. [Scalable Cross-Entropy, RecSys 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721), approximates full-catalog CE through GPU-efficient selection of informative outputs, reporting up to 100× lower peak memory than compared alternatives. [Correcting the LogQ Correction, 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) revisits sampling-probability correction for sampled softmax, making the correction itself an experimental consideration.\n\nHardest-negative selection needs controls: high-scoring unseen items may be potential positives. [R²NS, WWW 2026](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf), reports that premature hard mining can underperform uniform sampling; its framework combines uniform warm-up, approximate global candidate retrieval, and stochastic top-M selection with increasing difficulty. Practical experiment proposal: compare baseline BCE against multi-negative gBCE and sampled softmax, then test a uniform/hard mixture after warm-up. Mask padding, target collisions, and known training interactions; stochastic selection reduces reliance on potentially false negatives but cannot identify unknown positives reliably. Select using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 and GPU time, inspecting Electronics separately. Larger training margins alone would not demonstrate generalization."}
